bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-tiebreaker.prompt: Compute the least positive $x$ such that $25x-6$ is divisible by $1001$.

An integer $a$ is a quadratic nonresidue modulo a prime $p$ if there does not exist $x\in\mathbb Z$ such that $x^2\equiv a\pmod p$. How many ordered pairs $(a,b)$ modulo $29$ exist such that
$$a+b\equiv1\pmod{29}$$
where both $a$ and $b$ are quadratic nonresidues modulo $29$?
Let $f:\mathbb Z^2\to\mathbb C$ be a function such that $f(x+11,y)=f(x,y+11)=f(x,y)$, and $f(x,y)f(z,w)=f(xz-yw,xw+yz)$. How many possible values can $f(1,1)$ have?
